question:
Medini Rai of Chanderi, Hasan Khan of Mewat and Mahmud Lodi joined Rana Sanga with their forces to fight against which of the following Mughal rulers?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Babur
Akbar
Aurangzeb
Humayun
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Babur

Explanation:
Medini Rai (Chanderi), Hasan Khan (Mewat), and Mahmud Lodi (last ruler of the Lodi dynasty) allied with Rana Sanga to fight against Babur. This conflict took place in the Battle of Khanwa (1527), where Babur defeated this coalition. Rana Sanga had formed a Hindu-Muslim alliance against Babur, but Babur's superior tactics and artillery ensured his victory. This battle was a turning point in the establishment of the Mughal Empire in India.

Extra Facts:
The Battle of Khanwa was a decisive conflict between the Mughals and the Rajputs. Babur raised the morale of his army by declaring it a 'Jihad'. Rana Sanga, along with his allies, attempted to expel Babur from India but failed. After this battle, Mughal dominance was firmly established in North India.

question_hi:
चंदेरी के मेदिनी राय, मेवात के हसन खान और महमूद लोदी निम्नलिखित में से किस मुग़ल शासक के खिलाफ लड़ने के लिए अपनी सेना सहित राणा सांगा के साथ मिल गए थे?

अकबर
औरंगजेब
हुमायूँ
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बाबर

Explanation:
मेदिनी राय (चंदेरी), हसन खान (मेवात) और महमूद लोदी (लोदी वंश के अंतिम शासक) ने राणा सांगा के साथ मिलकर बाबर के खिलाफ युद्ध किया था। यह संघर्ष खानवा का युद्ध (1527) में हुआ था, जिसमें बाबर ने इन सभी शक्तियों को हराया। राणा सांगा ने बाबर के खिलाफ एक हिंदू-मुस्लिम गठबंधन बनाया था, लेकिन बाबर ने अपनी श्रेष्ठ रणनीति और तोपखाने के बल पर विजय प्राप्त की। यह युद्ध मुगल साम्राज्य की स्थापना में एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ साबित हुआ।

Extra Facts:
खानवा का युद्ध मुगलों और राजपूतों के बीच एक निर्णायक युद्ध था। बाबर ने इस युद्ध में 'जिहाद' का नारा देकर अपनी सेना का मनोबल बढ़ाया। राणा सांगा ने अपने सहयोगियों के साथ मिलकर बाबर को भारत से खदेड़ने का प्रयास किया, लेकिन असफल रहे। इस युद्ध के बाद मुगलों का प्रभुत्व उत्तर भारत में स्थापित हो गया।

question:
Jama Masjid in Delhi was built by_______.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Shah Jahan
Alauddin Khilji
Akbar
Sikandar Lodi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shah Jahan

Explanation:
The Jama Masjid in Delhi was built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1644 and 1656 CE. It is one of the largest mosques in India and a masterpiece of Mughal architecture. Constructed using red sandstone and white marble, it was part of Shah Jahan's new capital city, Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi). The mosque was designed by the chief architect Ustad Khalil.

Extra Facts:
The Jama Masjid is originally named 'Masjid-e-Jahan-Numa', meaning 'the mosque commanding a view of the world'. It can accommodate around 25,000 worshippers at a time. The main dome stands at a height of 41 meters, and its two minarets are 40 meters tall. Shah Jahan built this mosque as a significant architectural legacy of his reign.

question_hi:
दिल्ली में जामा मस्जिद द्वारा बनवाई गई थी।

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: शाहजहाँ
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी
अकबर
सिकंदर लोदी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है शाहजहाँ

Explanation:
जामा मस्जिद, दिल्ली का निर्माण मुग़ल बादशाह शाहजहाँ ने 1644 से 1656 ईस्वी के बीच करवाया था। यह मस्जिद भारत की सबसे बड़ी मस्जिदों में से एक है और मुग़ल वास्तुकला का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है। इसका निर्माण लाल बलुआ पत्थर और संगमरमर से किया गया है। शाहजहाँ ने इसे अपनी राजधानी शाहजहाँनाबाद (पुरानी दिल्ली) में बनवाया था। यह मस्जिद उस्ताद खलील नामक वास्तुकार द्वारा डिजाइन की गई थी।

Extra Facts:
जामा मस्जिद का वास्तविक नाम 'मस्जिद-ए-जहाँ-नुमा' है, जिसका अर्थ है 'दुनिया को दिखाने वाली मस्जिद'। यह मस्जिद लगभग 25,000 लोगों को एक साथ नमाज़ पढ़ने की सुविधा प्रदान करती है। इसके मुख्य गुंबद की ऊँचाई 41 मीटर है और इसके दो मीनारें 40 मीटर ऊँची हैं। शाहजहाँ ने इस मस्जिद को अपने शासनकाल की एक महत्वपूर्ण धरोहर के रूप में बनवाया था।

question:
The Mughal Empire was ruled by Jahangir during:

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: 1605-1627 CE
1601-1629 CE
1600-1630 CE
1603-1629 CE
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1605-1627 CE

Explanation:
Jahangir (Nur-ud-din Muhammad Salim) ruled the Mughal Empire from 1605 to 1627 CE. He was the son of Akbar and the father of Shah Jahan. His reign was marked by patronage of art, literature, and architecture. Key events during his rule include the arrival of Sir Thomas Roe (1615 CE) and the influence of Nur Jahan. He also wrote an autobiography, 'Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri', which is an important source of Mughal history.

Extra Facts:
Jahangir's reign is famous for the 'Chain of Justice', which he installed to ensure access to justice. He promoted painting and patronized artists like Mansur. His wife, Nur Jahan, played a significant political role, and coins were minted in her name.

question_hi:
मुगल साम्राज्य पर जहांगीर का शासन निम्न में से किस वर्ष के दौरान था?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options_hi: 1605-1627 CE
1601-1629 CE
1600-1630 CE
1603-1629 CE
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 1605-1627 ईस्वी

Explanation:
जहांगीर (नूरुद्दीन मोहम्मद सलीम) ने मुगल साम्राज्य पर 1605 से 1627 ईस्वी तक शासन किया। वह अकबर का पुत्र और शाहजहाँ का पिता था। उसने अपने शासनकाल में कला, साहित्य और वास्तुकला को प्रोत्साहित किया। जहांगीर के शासन की प्रमुख घटनाओं में सर थॉमस रो का भारत आगमन (1615 ईस्वी) और नूरजहाँ का प्रभाव शामिल है। उसने 'तुजुक-ए-जहांगीरी' नामक आत्मकथा भी लिखी, जो मुगल इतिहास का महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है।

Extra Facts:
जहांगीर के शासनकाल को 'न्याय की जंजीर' (Chain of Justice) के लिए जाना जाता है, जिसे उसने न्याय की पहुँच सुनिश्चित करने के लिए लगवाया था। उसने चित्रकला को बढ़ावा दिया और मंसूर जैसे प्रसिद्ध चित्रकारों को संरक्षण प्रदान किया। उसकी पत्नी नूरजहाँ ने राजनीति में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई और सिक्कों पर उसका नाम भी अंकित होता था।

question:
Tanse, one of the well-known musicians of medieval India, was in the court of which of the following Mughal emperors? SSC CHSL 31st May 2022 ( Morning)

[SSC CHSL 2021]
options: Akbar
Aurangzeb
Babur
Humayun
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
Tansen was one of the most famous musicians of medieval India and was one of the 'Navratnas' (Nine Jewels) in the court of the Mughal emperor Akbar. His original name was Ramtanu Pandey. Akbar bestowed upon him the title 'Miyan Tansen'. Tansen composed several new ragas, such as Miyan Ki Malhar, Darbari Kanada, etc. He is regarded as a great maestro of Indian classical music. His presence in Akbar's court enriched Mughal music.

Extra Facts:
Tansen was born in Gwalior and received his musical training from Haridas Swami. Due to his talent, he was highly respected in Akbar's court. Tansen popularized the Dhrupad style, and the ragas he composed remain famous even today. After his death, he was buried in Gwalior, where music festivals are still held at his tomb.

question_hi:

औरंगजेब
बाबर
हुमायूं

Explanation:
तानसेन मध्यकालीन भारत के सबसे प्रसिद्ध संगीतकारों में से एक थे, जो मुगल सम्राट अकबर के दरबार में 'नवरत्नों' में से एक थे। उनका वास्तविक नाम रामतनु पांडे था। अकबर ने उन्हें 'मियां तानसेन' की उपाधि दी थी। तानसेन ने कई नए रागों की रचना की, जैसे मियां की मल्हार, दरबारी कान्हड़ा, आदि। उन्हें भारतीय शास्त्रीय संगीत का एक महान संगीतज्ञ माना जाता है। अकबर के दरबार में उनकी उपस्थिति ने मुगल संगीत को समृद्ध किया।

Extra Facts:
तानसेन का जन्म ग्वालियर में हुआ था और उन्होंने हरिदास स्वामी से संगीत की शिक्षा प्राप्त की। अकबर के दरबार में उनकी प्रतिभा के कारण उन्हें विशेष सम्मान प्राप्त था। तानसेन ने ध्रुपद शैली को लोकप्रिय बनाया और उनके द्वारा रचित राग आज भी प्रसिद्ध हैं। उनकी मृत्यु के बाद, उन्हें ग्वालियर में दफनाया गया, जहां आज भी उनकी समाधि पर संगीत समारोह आयोजित किए जाते हैं।

question:
Which of the following was the first city planned by the Mughal Empire?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Fatehpur Sikri
Islamabad
Delhi
Agra
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fatehpur Sikri

Explanation:
Fatehpur Sikri was the first city planned by the Mughal Empire. It was established by Emperor Akbar in 1571 AD as his capital. This city is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture and was built in honor of the Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti. Fatehpur Sikri includes famous structures like the Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, and Diwan-i-Khas. However, due to water scarcity, Akbar had to abandon it in 1585, and the capital was shifted to Lahore.

Extra Facts:
Fatehpur Sikri was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986). The city also symbolizes the religious tolerance of the Mughal Empire, as it showcases a blend of Hindu and Islamic architecture. Akbar also proclaimed the Din-i-Ilahi religion here, which was a syncretic faith.

दिल्ली
आगरा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है फतेहपुर सीकरी

Explanation:
फतेहपुर सीकरी मुगल साम्राज्य द्वारा नियोजित पहला शहर था। इसे सम्राट अकबर ने 1571 ईस्वी में अपनी राजधानी के रूप में स्थापित किया था। यह शहर मुगल वास्तुकला का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है और इसे 'सूफी संत शेख सलीम चिश्ती' के सम्मान में बनवाया गया था। फतेहपुर सीकरी में प्रसिद्ध इमारतें जैसे बुलंद दरवाजा, जामा मस्जिद, पंच महल और दीवान-ए-खास शामिल हैं। हालांकि, पानी की कमी के कारण अकबर को 1585 में इसे छोड़ना पड़ा और राजधानी को लाहौर स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया।

Extra Facts:
फतेहपुर सीकरी को यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल (1986) घोषित किया गया है। यह शहर मुगल साम्राज्य की धार्मिक सहिष्णुता का प्रतीक भी है, क्योंकि इसमें हिंदू और इस्लामिक वास्तुकला का मिश्रण देखने को मिलता है। अकबर ने यहाँ दीन-ए-इलाही धर्म की भी घोषणा की थी, जो विभिन्न धर्मों का समन्वय था।

In which year was the construction of Jama Masjid of Delhi completed?

दिल्ली की जामा मस्जिद का निर्माण किस वर्ष पूरा हुआ था?

question:
In the context of economic system of Mughal Empire, the term 'Polaj' referred to

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: a type of coin introduced by Akbar
annually cultivated land
cash payment
a kind of tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is annually cultivated land

Explanation:
In the Mughal Empire's land revenue system, the term 'Polaj' referred to land that was cultivated every year. This type of land was highly fertile and considered suitable for continuous cultivation. The Mughals classified land based on productivity, with Polaj being the most fertile. Other categories included Parauti (cultivated once in two years), Chachar (cultivated once in three-four years), and Banjar (uncultivated for long periods). During Akbar's reign, his revenue minister Todar Mal implemented the 'Dahsala Bandobast' system, where higher revenue was collected from Polaj land.

Extra Facts:
The Mughal land revenue system was based on the Zabti system, where a fixed share of the produce was taken by the state. Akbar introduced the Ilahi Gaz for land measurement to standardize assessments. Sher Shah Suri had earlier introduced systems like Rai (direct tax collection from peasants) and Kankut (tax on estimated yield), which the Mughals later modified.

question_hi:
मुगल साम्राज्य की आर्थिक व्यवस्था के सन्दर्भ में 'पोलाज' शब्द का क्या उल्लेख है?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options_hi: अकबर द्वारा पेश किया गया एक प्रकार का सिक्का
सालाना खेती की भूमि
नकद भुगतान
एक प्रकार का कर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सालाना खेती की भूमि

Explanation:
मुगल काल में भूमि राजस्व व्यवस्था में 'पोलाज' शब्द का उल्लेख उस भूमि के लिए किया जाता था जिसे हर साल खेती के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता था। यह भूमि उपजाऊ होती थी और लगातार खेती के योग्य मानी जाती थी। मुगलों ने भूमि को उसकी उत्पादकता के आधार पर वर्गीकृत किया था, जिसमें पोलाज सबसे अधिक उपजाऊ भूमि थी। इसके अलावा, परौती (एक या दो साल में एक बार खेती), चचर (तीन-चार साल में एक बार खेती) और बंजर (लंबे समय तक खेती न की गई भूमि) जैसे अन्य प्रकार भी थे। अकबर के शासनकाल में राजस्व मंत्री टोडरमल ने 'दहसाला बंदोबस्त' लागू किया, जिसमें पोलाज भूमि से अधिक राजस्व वसूला जाता था।

Extra Facts:
मुगल काल में भूमि राजस्व प्रणाली ज़ब्ती प्रणाली पर आधारित थी, जिसमें उपज का एक निश्चित हिस्सा सरकार को दिया जाता था। अकबर ने भूमि माप के लिए इलाही गज का प्रयोग किया, जिससे मापन में एकरूपता आई। शेरशाह सूरी ने भी पहले ही राय (किसानों से सीधे कर वसूली) और कनकूत (अनुमानित उपज पर कर) जैसी प्रणालियाँ लागू की थीं, जिन्हें मुगलों ने संशोधित कर अपनाया।

question:
In how many books is 'Akbar Nama', written by Abul Fazal, divided?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Five
Four
Two
Three
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Three

Explanation:
The Akbar Nama, written by Abul Fazl, is a monumental historical text that chronicles the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar (1556-1605). It is divided into three books:
1. First Book - Covers Akbar’s ancestry, birth, and history up to 1602 CE.
2. Second Book - Known as ‘Ain-i-Akbari’, it details Akbar’s administration, land revenue system, socio-economic conditions, and cultural developments.
3. Third Book - Describes the final years of Akbar’s reign and his death.

Extra Facts:
The Akbar Nama was written in Persian and is one of the most significant documents of the Mughal era. Abul Fazl composed it under Akbar’s patronage, providing not just historical events but also cultural and administrative reforms.

question:
The art of decoration, called Pietra dura became popular during whose reign?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Jahangir
Sher Shah Suri
Shah Jahan
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shah Jahan

Explanation:
Pietra dura is an Italian decorative art form involving inlaid designs using cut colored stones. This art reached its peak during the reign of Shah Jahan (1628-1658 CE). Shah Jahan used this art extensively in monuments like the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Moti Masjid. The art reflects the grandeur and intricacy of Mughal architecture. During Shah Jahan's time, it was also called 'Parchin Kari'.

Extra Facts:
The Pietra dura technique was introduced to India by the Mughals from Persia and Italy. It primarily involved inlaying semi-precious stones like lapis lazuli, jasper, and mother-of-pearl into marble. Italian artisans in Shah Jahan's court further refined this art. The Taj Mahal is the most famous example of Pietra dura work, showcasing floral and geometric patterns.

पिएट्रा ड्यूरा कला को भारत में मुगलों द्वारा फारस और इटली से लाया गया था। यह कला मुख्य रूप से संगमरमर पर की जाती थी और इसमें अर्ध-कीमती पत्थरों जैसे लैपिस लाजुली, जैस्पर, मदर-ऑफ-पर्ल आदि का उपयोग होता था। शाहजहाँ के दरबार में इतालवी कलाकारों ने भी काम किया, जिन्होंने इस कला को और विकसित किया।

question:
The title 'Mirza Raja' was accorded by Aurangzeb to two of his highest-ranking nobles:

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Ratan Singh and Uday Singh II
Man Singh Tomar and Rana Kumbha
Jai Singh and Jaswant Singh
Govinda Chauhan and Rana Hammir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jai Singh and Jaswant Singh

Explanation:
Aurangzeb conferred the title 'Mirza Raja' upon two of his highest-ranking nobles: Jai Singh (Raja of Amber) and Jaswant Singh (Raja of Marwar). Jai Singh was a skilled Mughal commander who played a key role in campaigns against Shivaji. Jaswant Singh was also a prominent Mughal noble, though his relationship with Aurangzeb remained tense. This title was one of the highest honors given to Rajputs in the Mughal Empire, reflecting their loyalty and military contributions.

Extra Facts:
Jai Singh negotiated the Treaty of Purandar (1665), where Shivaji surrendered to the Mughals. Jaswant Singh was appointed governor of Kabul by Aurangzeb, but after his death, Aurangzeb annexed Marwar, leading to the Rathore-Mughal conflict.

question:
When was the Treaty of Purandar signed between Jai Singh I, commander of the Mughal Empire, and Shivaji?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: 1639
1702
1665
1681
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1665

Explanation:
The Treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665 CE between Jai Singh I, the Mughal commander, and the Maratha ruler Shivaji. This treaty came after prolonged conflicts between the Mughals and the Marathas. Jai Singh had besieged Shivaji, forcing him to agree to the treaty. As per the treaty, Shivaji surrendered 23 forts to the Mughals and agreed to send his son Sambhaji to the Mughal court. However, the treaty proved temporary, as Shivaji later rebelled against the Mughals again.

Extra Facts:
The Treaty of Purandar was a turning point in Maratha-Mughal relations. After this treaty, Shivaji was summoned to Agra to meet Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, where he was placed under house arrest. However, Shivaji cleverly escaped and revived the Maratha Empire.

question:
Ain-i-Akbari which is the third volume of the book ‘Akbar Nama’ deals with ______.

[SSC MTS ]
options: Akbar’s ancestors
Akbar’s events of Akbar’s reign
Akbar’s religion
Akbar’s administration
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar’s administration

Explanation:
Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of Akbar Nama, written by Abul Fazl. It primarily deals with Akbar’s administrative system, including detailed descriptions of the Mughal Empire's land revenue system, military organization, socio-economic conditions, art, culture, and various departments. This book is a crucial source for understanding medieval Indian history. The first two volumes of Akbar Nama cover Akbar’s ancestors and events of his reign, while the third volume (Ain-i-Akbari) focuses specifically on administrative details.

Extra Facts:
Akbar Nama was written in Persian and is one of the most important historical texts of the Mughal era. Abul Fazl was one of Akbar’s Navratnas (Nine Jewels) and composed this work under Akbar’s patronage. Ain-i-Akbari also mentions the Mansabdari system, Zabti revenue system, and Akbar’s religious policy (Din-i-Ilahi).

Alauddin Khalji's
Muhammad Tughluq's
Genghis Khan's
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sher Shah Suri's

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri (1540-1545 CE) established an efficient administrative system during his short reign, which was later adopted by Mughal emperor Akbar. Sher Shah introduced reforms like the land revenue system (Zabti system), postal services, road construction (Grand Trunk Road), and a strong military organization. Akbar consolidated the Mughal Empire by incorporating these administrative elements.

Extra Facts:
Sher Shah introduced the Rupee and Dam coins, which were continued by the Mughals. His justice system and police administration were also highly effective. Akbar’s revenue minister Todar Mal further refined Sher Shah’s land revenue system, known as the Dahsala system.

Who was the Mughal Emperor at the time of Battle of Plassey?

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alamgir II

Explanation:
The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757. At that time, the Mughal Emperor was Alamgir II (1754-1759). This battle was fought between the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, and the British East India Company. The British, led by Robert Clive, won this battle, which laid the foundation of British rule in India. Alamgir II was a weak ruler, and during his reign, the decline of the Mughal Empire accelerated.

Extra Facts:
The Battle of Plassey was the first major step in the expansion of British power in India. After this battle, the British established dominance over Bengal. Mir Jafar, who betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah, was made the Nawab. This battle became a symbol of 'conspiracy and betrayal'.

question:
The Battle of Khanwa was fought between:

[SSC MTS ]
options: Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
Babur and Rana Sangha
Sher Shah Suri and Rana Sangha
Babur and Sher Shah Suri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Babur and Rana Sanga

Explanation:
The Battle of Khanwa was fought on 17 March 1527 between Babur and Rana Sanga of Mewar. This battle was a turning point in the establishment of the Mughal Empire in India. Babur used innovative tactics like the 'Tulughma' and 'Rumi' strategies to secure victory. Rana Sanga had formed a grand alliance of Rajputs and other local rulers but failed to withstand Babur's forces. After this battle, Babur adopted the title 'Ghazi' and solidified Mughal dominance in North India.

Extra Facts:
The Battle of Khanwa occurred after the First Battle of Panipat (1526), where Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi. Rana Sanga aimed to expel Babur from India but was unsuccessful. Post this battle, Rajput power declined, and Mughal influence grew significantly.

Extra Facts:
The Mughal court patronized art and culture extensively. Akbar encouraged not only painters but also calligraphers. Calligraphy, known as 'Ilm-e-Khushnavisi,' was a highly respected art form during the Mughal era.

question:
Who introduced the Mansabdari system into the administration under the Mughals?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Akbar
Shah Jahan
Aurangzeb
Jahangir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
The Mansabdari system was introduced into the Mughal administration by Akbar . This system was a crucial part of the military and civil administration of the Mughal Empire. Mansabdars were appointed based on their 'zat' (rank) and 'sawar' (number of cavalrymen). Under this system, Mansabdars received either cash salaries or 'jagirs' (revenue assignments). Akbar implemented it in the 1570s, which improved administrative efficiency and military organization. This system played a vital role in the stability and expansion of the Mughal Empire.

Extra Facts:
The Mansabdari system was a unique administrative policy of the Mughals, integrating military and civil officials into a single hierarchy. Akbar linked it with the Zabt system (revenue management) to make it more effective. Mansabdars could be promoted or demoted based on their performance, leading to a centralized and disciplined administrative structure.

Extra Facts:
मनसबदारी व्यवस्था मुगलों की एक अनूठी प्रशासनिक नीति थी, जिसमें सैन्य और नागरिक अधिकारियों को एक ही पदानुक्रम में रखा गया था। अकबर ने इसे ज़ाब्ता प्रणाली (राजस्व प्रबंधन) के साथ जोड़कर और अधिक प्रभावी बनाया। इस व्यवस्था के तहत, मनसबदारों को उनकी सेवाओं के अनुसार पदोन्नति या पदावनति की जा सकती थी। इससे एक केंद्रीकृत और अनुशासित प्रशासनिक ढाँचा विकसित हुआ।

question:
During the reign of Akbar, _________ was the land that has lain fallow for three or four years.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Parauti
Polaj
Chachar
Banjar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chachar

Explanation:
During Akbar's reign, land was classified based on its productivity. Chachar referred to land that had been left fallow for three or four years. Although uncultivated during this period, it could be reclaimed for agriculture. Akbar's revenue minister, Todar Mal, implemented the Zabti System (Mansabdari system), which categorized land into Polaj (continuously cultivated), Parauti (fallow for 1-2 years), Chachar (fallow for 3-4 years), and Banjar (fallow for five or more years). This classification was crucial for tax assessment.

Extra Facts:
Akbar introduced the Dahsala System (taxation based on 10-year average yield). Todar Mal used Gaz-i-Sikandari (a measuring unit) for land surveys. Akbar's revenue policies stabilized farmers and boosted agricultural output.

Explanation:

The battle took place near Haldighati, a mountain pass in Rajasthan's Aravalli Range. The Mughal army was commanded by Man Singh I and Asaf Khan, while Rana Pratap led a smaller force of Rajput warriors. Although the Mughals claimed victory, Rana Pratap refused to submit to Akbar and continued his resistance through guerrilla warfare. The battle is remembered for the bravery of Rana Pratap and his loyal horse Chetak, who died in the battle.

Extra Facts:
The Battle of Haldighati is a symbol of Rajput resistance against Mughal expansion. Despite being outnumbered, Rana Pratap's forces displayed immense courage. Chetak, Rana Pratap's horse, became legendary for its loyalty and sacrifice. Even after the battle, Mewar remained unconquered, and Rana Pratap continued to fight for independence until his death.

Extra Facts:
हल्दीघाटी युद्ध को भारतीय इतिहास में एक प्रतीकात्मक संघर्ष के रूप में देखा जाता है, जहाँ एक छोटी सी सेना ने विशाल मुगल साम्राज्य का सामना किया। राणा प्रताप का घोड़ा चेतक इस युद्ध में वीरगति को प्राप्त हुआ, जिसे आज भी वीरता का प्रतीक माना जाता है। युद्ध के बाद भी मेवाड़ पर मुगलों का पूर्ण नियंत्रण नहीं हो पाया और राणा प्रताप ने अपने जीवन के अंतिम समय तक स्वतंत्रता के लिए संघर्ष जारी रखा।

question:
Which of the following is (Under Mughal ruler-Foreign traveller visited India)- correctly matched?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Aurangzeb- Manucci
Shah Jahan- William Hawkins
Jahangir- Manucci
Akbar- Sir Thomas Roe
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Aurangzeb-Manucci

Explanation:
Niccolao Manucci was an Italian traveller who visited India during Aurangzeb's reign (1656-1707 CE). He wrote 'Storia do Mogor', detailing the Mughal court and Aurangzeb's rule. Other options are incorrect: William Hawkins came to Jahangir's court (1608-11 CE), Sir Thomas Roe was an English ambassador during Jahangir's time (1615-18 CE), and Manucci never visited Shah Jahan or Jahangir's courts.

Extra Facts:
Manucci described Aurangzeb's religious orthodoxy and Deccan campaigns. His accounts help understand the decline of the Mughal Empire. William Hawkins attempted trade negotiations with Jahangir, while Sir Thomas Roe secured trading rights for the English in Surat.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा (मुगल शासक के अधीन-विदेशी यात्री भारत आया)- सही सुमेलित है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: औरंगजेब-मनुची
शाहजहां- विलियम हॉकिन्स
जहांगीर-मनुची
अकबर- सर थॉमस रो
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है औरंगजेब-मनुची

Explanation:
निकोलाओ मनुची एक इतालवी यात्री था जो औरंगजेब के शासनकाल (1656-1707 ई.) में भारत आया था। उसने 'स्टोरिया डो मोगोर' नामक पुस्तक लिखी, जिसमें मुगल दरबार और औरंगजेब के शासन का विस्तृत वर्णन है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: विलियम हॉकिन्स जहांगीर के दरबार में आया था (1608-11 ई.), सर थॉमस रो जहांगीर के समय (1615-18 ई.) में आया, और मनुची कभी शाहजहां या जहांगीर के दरबार में नहीं गया।

Extra Facts:
मनुची ने औरंगजेब के धार्मिक कट्टरता और दक्कन अभियानों का विवरण दिया। उसका लेखन मुगल साम्राज्य के पतन के कारणों को समझने में मदद करता है। विलियम हॉकिन्स ने जहांगीर के साथ व्यापारिक समझौते की कोशिश की, जबकि सर थॉमस रो ने अंग्रेजों को सूरत में फैक्ट्री स्थापित करने का अधिकार दिलाया।
